title: Hot/Cold prefix stratification and GPU page-aware eviction hints for continuous batching
creator: Asha Kulkarni
description: Problem: Under mixed workloads we observe that small conversational prefixes are frequently re-used while large system prompts and rare long contexts pollute GPU slab space. This increases GPU memory pressure, forces premature eviction of useful KV fragments, and hurts batching efficiency (more cold misses and higher tail latency). Goal: introduce a light-weight runtime-level stratification that marks prefix fragments as hot or cold, emit GPU-page-aware eviction hints, and expose affinity signals into the continuous-batcher so that batches preserve reuse locality and reduce redundant KV loads.
proposal: 1) Runtime telemetry: extend KV fragment metadata with a hot_score (decay-based) and residency_hint (GPU page id estimate) emitted at fragment write and on reuse. 2) Hot/Cold allocator: maintain two slab pools per GPU: hot-resident slabs (short retention but pinned for faster reuse) and cold-evictable slabs (higher eviction priority). 3) Page-aware eviction hints: when eviction candidate chosen, annotate with approximate GPU page ranges to prefer evicting contiguous cold pages and avoid scattering hot fragments. 4) Batch affinity signals: continuous-batcher will prefer grouping requests that touch overlapping hot fragment sets for the next window, and optionally delay low-priority cold loads to burst windows. 5) Backward compat: implement feature flag at per-tenant level and fall back to current LRU-style flow if disabled.
alternatives: A. Purely probabilistic bloom-based dedupe without hot/cold separation — simpler but leads to noisy retention of large cold fragments.
B. Global TTL per fragment — easy but too coarse for workloads with strong reuse skew.
C. Full content-addressable store for all prefixes — high memory overhead and CPU hashing cost; longer-term option but not suitable short term.
risks: Extra metadata increases memory overhead per fragment — mitigate by compacting hot_score into a single byte and sampling updates.
Incorrect page-id estimation could cause suboptimal evictions — mitigate by conservative estimates and validation in canary.
Batch affinity could increase tail latency for non-affine requests if not throttled — control via priority knobs and max-delay SLO.
test_plan: Unit tests for hot_score decay, residency_hint serialization, and allocator APIs
Simulation on request replay traces comparing baseline vs hot/cold strategy (metrics: GPU mem used, token/sec, p95/p99 latency, KV load rate)
Canary in staging with 10% traffic across 2 tenants (one chat-heavy, one search-heavy) and automatic rollback on >5% tail-latency regression
Integration tests for continuous-batcher affinity signals and correctness under preemption/fallback scenarios
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind tenant flag and runtime config; start with read-only telemetry for 1 week to validate signals
Enable hot/cold allocation in staging with 5% of GPUs for 2 weeks, collect metrics, iterate
Gradual rollout to production by tenant: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring alerts and a kill-switch
Post-rollout: run eviction-heatmap job weekly and export slab compaction savings to cost dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Stable hot_score telemetry with <10% sampling error vs full-trace baseline
>=15% reduction in KV load rate for chat-heavy tenant under identical traffic
No more than 3% regression in p50 latency and no regression in p99 beyond configured SLO during canary
GPU memory churn (pages evicted per minute) reduced by >=20% on targeted workloads
